why_this_cell: The FOURTH production-ready cell, and the one that was impossible until app/py_codemod.py existed. The registry listed it as blocked on nothing but a fixture; a fixture written against the old handler would have failed at the typecheck step, because the handler was a no-op that reported success. That is the registry working as intended -- 'blocked on a fixture' names the next thing to try, not a guarantee it passes.

expect.fix_target_note: The USAGES are stale, not the declaration -- the opposite of both change-field-type cells. src/models.py is regenerated from the new spec and is already correct, so touching it would mean the codemod went after the declaration instead of the usages. Same relationship as the TypeScript remove-field cell.

hazards.hazard: mypy's reach depends on the CONSUMER's annotations
hazards.fixture_requirement: Every def in this fixture is annotated. An unannotated def would make the verdict UNABLE_TO_VALIDATE rather than VALID -- mypy could not see the type of `user`, so both attribute errors would be invisible and a later pass would prove nothing. The test asserts mypy_annotation_gaps == 0 before the fix for exactly this reason.

hazards.hazard: Only some shapes are removable; the rest must abstain
hazards.fixture_requirement: Both references here are shapes py_codemod EDITS. A function parameter, an aliased local, a tuple unpacking, a keyword argument or a subscript would be REFUSED -- correctly -- and this cell would not qualify. That is the intended behaviour, not a fixture limitation.

hazards.hazard: The blank-line normaliser used to reformat every gap in the file
hazards.measured: _clean_blank_lines claimed to collapse 3+ blank lines to 2 but its regex collapsed them to ONE. PEP 8 requires two between top-level definitions, so every Python fix arrived as a diff touching every function boundary. Fixed to match the docstring; the test asserts blank-line runs are unchanged.

codemod_history.what_the_old_handler_did: Five context-free regexes. Measured on this fixture's own consumer: every reference survived, one blank-line run was collapsed, and it reported "Removed references to field 'phone_number' (2 lines affected). Cleaned: struct/class declarations, accessor methods, function params, object literals, and direct field access patterns for python." Two false claims in one string -- nothing was removed, and the five named categories were a fixed list appended to every success regardless of what happened.
codemod_history.why_that_was_worse_than_a_no_op: `changed` was True because whitespace differed, so the pipeline believed a fix existed and only the validator stood between that and a PR.
two_regexes_were_destructive_not_useless: r'\b{f}\s*:\s*[^,=)]+(\s*=[^,)]+)?\s*,?\s*' stripped a FUNCTION PARAMETER -- the shape ts_codemod explicitly refuses, because it breaks every caller
r'^\s*.*\[\s*["\']?{f}["\']?\s*\].*$\n?' deleted the WHOLE LINE containing a subscript, taking the assignment and any call on it
